basic_information.name: LightRAG
basic_information.creator: Data Intelligence Lab @ The University of Hong Kong (HKUDS) — led by Prof. Chao Huang. Authors: Zirui Guo, Lianghao Xia, Yanhua Yu, Tu Ao, Chao Huang.
basic_information.description: LightRAG is a lightweight, graph-enhanced retrieval-augmented generation framework that integrates knowledge graph structures into text indexing and retrieval. During ingestion, it extracts entities and relations from text chunks using an LLM and builds a knowledge graph, then embeds both entities and relations as vectors. At query time, it employs a dual-level retrieval system — low-level retrieval targets specific entities and their direct relationships for precise factual queries, while high-level retrieval aggregates broader themes across multiple entities for synthesis questions. A hybrid mode combines both. Compared to Microsoft's GraphRAG, LightRAG achieves comparable or superior accuracy at roughly 1/100th the token cost per query (~100 tokens vs ~610,000), with incremental graph updates that avoid full reconstruction. Published at EMNLP 2025 Findings, it has rapidly become one of the most popular open-source RAG frameworks.
basic_information.release_date: October 2024 (arXiv preprint: 2410.05779); EMNLP 2025 Findings publication; PyPI latest version 1.4.9.11 released January 15, 2026

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Library/framework with optional API server. Core is a Python library (lightrag-hku on PyPI) that can run locally or as a Docker-based server with REST API and Web UI. Modular storage backends allow swapping graph, vector, and key-value stores independently.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports configurable embedding models. Recommended models: BAAI/bge-m3 (1024d) and OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (3072d). Any embedding model compatible with the configured provider can be used.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Knowledge graph-based indexing: LLM extracts entities and relations from each text chunk in a single pass, building a graph where nodes are entities and edges are typed, weighted relationships. Entity and relation descriptions are then embedded as vectors for retrieval. Vector storage supports FAISS, Chroma, Milvus, and other backends. The dual-level retrieval uses vector similarity on entity embeddings (low-level) and relation/theme embeddings (high-level).
technical_architecture.scalability: Supports incremental graph updates — new documents are processed and merged into the existing graph by adding/updating nodes and edges without full reconstruction. Storage backends include PostgreSQL, Neo4j, MongoDB, Redis, Milvus, and Chroma, enabling horizontal scaling. Neo4j recommended for production graph storage over PostgreSQL AGE. Metadata can grow unbounded with continuous ingestion (known scaling concern).
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Self-hosted via pip install (lightrag-hku), Docker / Docker Compose, offline/air-gapped deployment supported. LightRAG Server provides REST API + Web UI. No managed cloud offering — entirely self-hosted open-source.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dual-level graph-enhanced retrieval: (1) Low-level — vector similarity search on entity embeddings + direct relationship traversal for precise factual queries; (2) High-level — vector similarity on relation/theme embeddings aggregating broader conceptual patterns across multiple entities; (3) Hybrid mode — combines both low-level and high-level retrieval for comprehensive coverage. Also supports keyword-based search. The retrieved context (entities, relations, and associated text chunks) is assembled and passed to the LLM for generation.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Default text chunking with configurable chunk sizes. Through RAG-Anything integration (from HKUDS), supports multimodal document parsing with structure-aware chunking that preserves document hierarchy, tables, images, and formulas. The core LightRAG framework focuses on entity-relation extraction from chunks rather than advanced chunking strategies per se.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in reranker support, enabled by default. Recommended models: BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3, Jina rerankers. When a reranker is configured, 'mix' (hybrid) query mode is recommended as default. Warning issued if reranking is enabled without a configured rerank model.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Native multimodal support added June 2025 via RAG-Anything integration. Handles PDFs, Office documents (DOC/DOCX/PPT/PPTX/XLS/XLSX), images, tables, mathematical formulas. Builds multimodal knowledge graphs with cross-modal entity extraction and relationships.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: Core feature. LLM-based entity and relation extraction from text chunks in a single pass per chunk. Constructs a knowledge graph with typed, weighted relationships (relationship_strength scores). Supports graph visualization in the Web UI. Storage backends: Neo4j (recommended for production), PostgreSQL AGE, NetworkX (in-memory). Incremental graph updates without full reconstruction.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Citation functionality added March 2025. Supports source attribution via the include_chunk_content parameter, which returns actual retrieved chunk content in references. Two-step grounding: semantic vector search + relationship-based KG querying ensures LLM responses are grounded in verifiable information rather than speculative content.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Recommends LLMs with at least 32KB context (64KB preferred). Token-efficient retrieval: queries typically require <100 tokens of retrieval overhead (vs 610K for GraphRAG). Global context limit of 8MB for LLM queries. The graph structure inherently compresses information by storing entities and relations rather than raw text, reducing context window consumption.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Query latency ~80ms (approximately 30% reduction compared to standard RAG at ~120ms). Queries run 20-30ms faster than comparable systems. Update operations complete in roughly half the time of GraphRAG.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Single API call per retrieval query. During indexing, one LLM call per chunk for entity/relation extraction. Incremental updates process only new/changed documents. Specific QPS benchmarks not published in the paper.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Evaluated on 4 dimensions: Comprehensiveness, Diversity, Empowerment, and Overall. Win rates vs NaiveRAG across datasets — Agriculture: 67%/76%/67%, CS: 61%/62%/61%, Legal: 83%/86%/83%, Mix: 61%/67%/57%. On the Legal dataset, comprehension win rate improved from 16.4% (NaiveRAG) to 83.6% (LightRAG). Independent evaluation found smaller but still positive win rates (39.06% vs NaiveRAG on Agriculture, compared to originally reported 66.70%).
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: Outperforms NaiveRAG, RQ-RAG, HyDE, and GraphRAG across all four evaluation dimensions on Agriculture, CS, Legal, and Mix datasets. Uses LLM-based evaluation (GPT-4 as judge). Token efficiency: ~100 tokens per query vs GraphRAG's ~610,000 tokens. Independent replication studies show gains are real but potentially smaller than originally reported.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Standalone framework (not a plugin for LangChain/LlamaIndex). However, integrations exist: LlamaIndex module for async chat completions and embedding generation within LightRAG; LangChain-compatible model loading. DSPy and Haystack integrations not natively available. The framework is self-contained with its own orchestration pipeline.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-4o), Anthropic (Claude 3.5+), Google, Mistral, open-source models via Ollama (LLaMA, Qwen, etc.), Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, HuggingFace models. Recommends LLMs with at least 32B parameters for reliable entity-relation extraction. Embedding: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large, BAAI/bge-m3, and any configurable provider.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Community MCP server available (Daniel LightRAG MCP Server, published January 2026). Provides 22 tools across 4 categories: document management, querying, knowledge graph operations, system management. Requires local LightRAG server running. Not an official HKUDS integration.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Document ingestion via file upload (text, PDF, Office documents via RAG-Anything). REST API for programmatic ingestion. No native connectors for Confluence, Notion, Slack, S3, or databases — documents must be provided as files or text. Web crawling possible via community integrations (Browser-use + LightRAG).
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Langfuse integration available via pip install lightrag-hku[observability]. Automatically traces all OpenAI-compatible LLM calls. Limitation: only OpenAI-compatible API calls are traced; Ollama, Azure, and AWS Bedrock not yet supported for Langfuse observability. No native OpenTelemetry, LangSmith, or Arize Phoenix integration.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Fully open-source and free (MIT license). No commercial pricing. Costs are only for underlying infrastructure: LLM API calls (entity extraction during indexing + generation during queries), embedding API calls, and storage/compute for graph and vector databases.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Entirely free and open-source. No usage limits imposed by LightRAG itself.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Dramatically cheaper than GraphRAG: processing documents costs ~$0.15 vs $4-7 for GraphRAG. Retrieval uses <100 tokens per query vs 610,000 for GraphRAG (6,000x reduction). Indexing cost is one LLM call per chunk for entity/relation extraction. Incremental updates avoid full graph reconstruction, saving significant reprocessing costs. Main cost driver is the LLM provider (OpenAI GPT-4o, etc.).
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Infrastructure costs: LLM API for indexing (1 call/chunk) + embedding API for entity/relation vectors + storage backend (Neo4j, PostgreSQL, or simpler options). For a startup: Neo4j Community Edition is free; embedding costs with OpenAI ~$0.13/1M tokens; GPT-4o for extraction ~$2.50/1M input tokens. A 10,000-document corpus might cost $5-20 to index depending on document length and LLM choice. Query costs are minimal (<100 tokens retrieval overhead). Self-hosted open-source models (Ollama + LLaMA 70B) can reduce ongoing costs to near-zero beyond compute.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Emerging leader in graph-enhanced RAG. One of the most popular open-source RAG frameworks globally with ~28K GitHub stars. Positioned as the lightweight, cost-effective alternative to Microsoft GraphRAG. Academic origin (EMNLP 2025) gives it strong research credibility. Part of the HKUDS ecosystem which has accumulated 77K+ total GitHub stars across projects.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: No specific named enterprise customers publicly disclosed (academic open-source project). Reported use cases include: customer support automation (e-commerce, telecom), enterprise knowledge management (manufacturing, logistics, insurance), legal and healthcare summarization, edge-AI for industrial IoT, and R&D in pharma/automotive/aerospace. Strong adoption in the developer and research community.
adoption_and_market.community_size: ~28,200 GitHub stars, ~4,000 forks, 300+ contributors. Active GitHub Issues (1,900+ issues, many open). PyPI package lightrag-hku with regular releases. Community MCP server and multiple third-party integrations. Trending on GitHub 15 times in its first year.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Academic open-source project from The University of Hong Kong — no venture funding or commercial entity. Prof. Chao Huang's Data Intelligence Lab is the maintaining organization. No commercial spin-off announced as of February 2026.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Main competitors: (1) Microsoft GraphRAG — more thorough graph analysis via community detection but dramatically more expensive (6,000x more tokens) and slower; (2) NaiveRAG/standard vector RAG — simpler but lacks relationship understanding; (3) E2GraphRAG — newer streamlined GraphRAG variant; (4) MiniRAG (also from HKUDS) — even more lightweight for small LLMs; (5) RAGFlow, R2R — full-stack RAG platforms with different trade-offs. LightRAG differentiates on: cost efficiency, incremental updates, dual-level retrieval, and simplicity of deployment.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Excellent fit for startups building knowledge-intensive applications (legal tech, healthcare, customer support, enterprise search) that need relationship-aware retrieval without GraphRAG's cost. Best for: teams of 2-5 engineers, budgets where LLM API costs matter, use cases with interconnected domain knowledge (e.g., regulatory compliance, medical literature, supply chain). The MIT license allows unrestricted commercial use. Requires Python expertise and comfort with self-hosting. Not ideal for teams wanting a fully managed, zero-ops solution.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Build with LightRAG when: you need graph-enhanced retrieval, cost control matters, your data has rich entity relationships, and you have engineering capacity to self-host. Use a managed RAG service (Pinecone + LangChain, or R2R/Dify) when: you need faster time-to-market, zero infrastructure management, or your use case doesn't benefit from knowledge graphs. LightRAG fills the middle ground — more capable than naive RAG, much cheaper than GraphRAG, but requires self-hosting and LLM configuration.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 1-3 days (pip install, configure LLM, ingest documents, query). Production: 1-2 weeks including storage backend setup (Neo4j/PostgreSQL), Docker deployment, API integration, reranker configuration, and testing. Add 1 week for multimodal document support via RAG-Anything. Ongoing: monitoring via Langfuse, incremental index updates as new documents arrive.
key_lessons: Graph-enhanced RAG does not have to be expensive: LightRAG proves you can get relationship-aware retrieval at 1/100th the cost of GraphRAG by using entity/relation vector embeddings instead of community detection

Dual-level retrieval is a powerful pattern: separating low-level (specific entity) and high-level (thematic/cross-entity) retrieval allows a single system to handle both precise factual queries and broad synthesis questions

Incremental updates are critical for production: unlike GraphRAG which requires full graph reconstruction, LightRAG merges new nodes/edges into the existing graph, making it viable for continuously growing knowledge bases

LLM quality matters more than architecture: LightRAG recommends 32B+ parameter models for entity extraction — using smaller models degrades the knowledge graph quality, which cascades into retrieval quality

Start simple, add graphs when needed: for many use cases, naive vector RAG is sufficient. Add LightRAG when you observe that your queries require understanding relationships between concepts that simple chunk retrieval misses
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Web UI available via LightRAG Server — provides document upload, knowledge graph visualization, and RAG query interface through an intuitive dashboard. Not a full no-code pipeline builder, but sufficient for non-technical users to interact with an existing LightRAG deployment.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (advanced RAG patterns and tools) and Session 3 (AI project frameworks — build vs buy, architecture decisions)

confidence.data_quality: High — based on peer-reviewed EMNLP 2025 Findings paper (arXiv 2410.05779), official GitHub repository, PyPI package metadata, and multiple independent technical analyses.
confidence.cross_reference: Paper available on arXiv, ACL Anthology, Semantic Scholar, and HuggingFace Papers. GitHub statistics confirmed across multiple sources. Cost comparisons validated by independent blog analyses (RagdollAI, LearnOpenCV, AnalyticsVidhya, PromptEngineering.org). Neo4j blog provides independent technical deep-dive. Independent evaluation (arxiv 2506.06331) confirms gains but notes potentially smaller effect sizes than originally reported.
confidence.caveats: Independent replication shows LightRAG's win rates may be smaller than originally reported in the paper (39% vs 67% on Agriculture). Entity extraction quality is heavily dependent on LLM capability — smaller models may produce poor knowledge graphs. Metadata can grow unbounded with continuous ingestion, causing performance degradation. Observability is limited to OpenAI-compatible APIs. No managed cloud offering means operational burden falls on the user. The project evolves rapidly (frequent PyPI releases) so APIs and features may change.
confidence.security_posture: SQL injection vulnerabilities in PostgreSQL storage were identified and patched. Knowledge graph structure can expose sensitive entity relationships — access controls and encryption recommended for production. Sending documents to external LLM APIs poses data governance risks for regulated industries; on-premise deployment with self-hosted models recommended in such cases. No built-in authentication/authorization for the API server — must be added at the infrastructure level. React Server Components vulnerability was fixed. General RAG risks apply: embedding inversion attacks, vector database exposure, overly broad retrieval matching.
